title: TaxGPT vs Hive Tax AI: Research Tool or Full Tax OS?
summary: TaxGPT vs Hive Tax AI: compare research depth, tax planning, tax writer, SALT research, return review, and prep automation to pick the right fit for your firm.
body_markdown:
## What Each Platform Is Built to Do


The clearest way to compare TaxGPT and Hive Tax AI isn't research quality versus research quality. It's scope. Hive picked two jobs and built for them specifically. TaxGPT built for the whole engagement, start to finish.


### Hive Tax AI – Research and Planning


Hive is built around two SKUs: a research assistant and a planning product, and both show the benefit of narrow scope. The research tool draws from a genuinely specific primary-source list rather than a generic web crawl, and it routes queries across models depending on the question, which is a sensible way to handle the tradeoffs between speed and depth on tax research specifically. The planning product sits on top of that research with a curated strategy library, built for practitioners who need to move from "what does the code say" to "what should this client do" without switching tools.


For a firm whose work stops at research and planning, that focus is a real strength, not a limitation to explain away.


### TaxGPT – The AI Operating System, Built for the Full Engagement


TaxGPT's scope starts in the same place, research, but doesn't stop there, and it starts from a stronger base: an in-house built tax code library that TaxGPT maintains directly, rather than licensing or aggregating from outside sources. Cowork extends into agentic prep workflows. Agent Andrew reviews completed returns rather than treating return analysis as an input to planning. TaxGPT Writer drafts memos, notice responses, engagement and opinion letters, and client emails. Client Intelligence carries context across a client relationship instead of resetting with every session. Planning lives inside this system too, through Cowork's Tax Planning Strategy workflow, drawing on the same client history and research base rather than starting from a blank slate.


That's the structural difference from Hive's two SKUs: Hive built two products. TaxGPT built one platform that covers research and planning on top of its own tax code library, plus everything a practitioner does after the research is done.


Hive picked two jobs and built for them cleanly. TaxGPT built for the same two jobs, on top of its own tax code library and client history, then extended into everything a practitioner does after the research and the plan: prep, review, drafting, and record-keeping. Firms whose work stays inside research and planning will find both platforms capable there. Firms whose work runs past that point have one platform covering the full engagement.


## Research Head-to-Head


Research is where TaxGPT and Hive Tax AI overlap most directly, and it's the section worth scrutinizing hardest, because it's the one place both platforms are making essentially the same claim: cite primary authority, don't hallucinate the answer.


Both platforms achieve this, but the foundation underneath the citation is different. TaxGPT's[AI tax research](https://taxgpt.com/ai-tax-research) runs on an in-house built tax code library, IRC sections, Treasury regulations, revenue rulings, and case law, maintained and updated directly rather than licensed or aggregated from a third party, layered with state, local, territorial, and treaty coverage. In[benchmark testing](https://www.taxgpt.com/blog/taxgpt-is-state-of-the-art-tax-llm) against leading general-purpose AI models on real-world tax scenarios, TaxGPT scored 96% accuracy with a 0% source hallucination rate. Hive's research product pulls from a curated primary-source list rather than a generic crawl, and its smart model routing, sending different question types to different models, plus weekly accuracy testing against known answers, is credible engineering. Both platforms avoid the generic-crawl problem; the difference is that TaxGPT owns and maintains its source library directly, rather than curating from external data.


Where the two diverge is jurisdictional breadth and what happens once the citation is in hand.


On breadth: Hive covers US federal and state. TaxGPT adds Canada, CRA guidance, the Income Tax Act, and provincial rules, plus Matrix's exportable multi-state grids for practitioners tracking a position across several states at once. For a firm with any cross-border or multi-state footprint, that gap compounds fast: one research pass in TaxGPT versus several manual ones stitched together elsewhere.


On what happens after the answer: this is really the throughline for the[common tax research challenges](https://taxgpt.com/blog/7-tax-research-challenges) practitioners run into with point tools generally, the research is only half the job. In Hive, the answer lives in the chat. In TaxGPT, the same answer can flow directly into a drafted memo, get attached to a client's record in Client Intelligence, or feed into a Cowork workflow already in motion. That's the[defensible tax research](https://taxgpt.com/blog/defensible-tax-research-vs-tax-research-tools) distinction worth naming directly: a citation is necessary but not sufficient if it dead-ends in a chat window instead of becoming part of the file.


## Tax Planning: Where the Two Approaches Diverge


Hive built a Planning Assistant. Upload a return or complete a questionnaire, and computer vision scans the return into a visual summary before an agentic workflow produces strategies from a library of curated options, with implementation guidance, savings calculations, citations, and risk assessments, delivered as a client-ready report on your letterhead.


TaxGPT approaches planning as agentic workflows rather than one product: strategy memos, savings opportunity scans, entity structure reviews, and interactive projection models. The difference that matters to a reviewing partner is what happens underneath. The agent builds a facts inventory citing the exact line and schedule for every figure, runs the return through twelve planning lenses rather than matching against a strategy list, and holds every citation to a verifiable standard: each code section, regulation, and threshold has to resolve to a live link on an authoritative federal domain, and anything it can't confirm is quarantined rather than published. Savings are computed after QBI, NIIT, AMT, SE tax, and state conformity, with unverified strategies excluded from the total. Strategies the math doesn't support are surfaced by the workflow with the rejection math shown, which is exactly the question a client asks in the meeting.


## Everything After the Plan


Research and planning are where Hive Tax AI competes. They're also where the comparison ends, because after the plan is written, the actual engagement is still mostly ahead: the return has to get prepared, the finished return has to get reviewed, correspondence has to go out, and someone has to remember what happened last year. This is where the platforms stop looking similar.


### Tax Prep


Cowork's agentic workflows operate directly inside tax software to prepare returns, not just gather the inputs for one. Hive has no return prep capability; a firm using it moves the return into separate tax software once the planning stage ends.


### Review


Agent Andrew is an AI tax return review software that reviews completed returns, not just return data feeding a planning recommendation. It works across 1040, 1041, 1065, 1120, and 1120-S returns, flagging issues on a Red/Green/Cleared basis so a reviewer knows exactly what needs attention before signing off. Hive's return analysis is a different thing entirely: it reads the return to select a planning strategy, then stops. That's the facts-table distinction worth being precise about, Hive extracts facts from a return to feed a recommendation engine; TaxGPT reviews a completed return as its own deliverable, a distinction also covered in[manual review vs AI return review](https://www.taxgpt.com/taxgpt-insights/manual-tax-review-vs-agent-andrew) .


### Drafting Breadth


Writer drafts notice responses, engagement letters, opinion letters, and client emails, correspondence that spans the practice, not just the research file. Hive's memo drafting stays scoped to the research product: memos that document a research answer, not the broader set of documents a firm sends clients and taxing authorities over the course of an engagement.


### Client Memory


Client Intelligence persists context across sessions and years, so a returning client's history informs the next research query, the next plan, the next review. Hive has no equivalent; each engagement starts without that accumulated context.


Run the math on the actual workflow: research plus planning gets a firm a strategy. It doesn't get the return prepared, doesn't get it reviewed, and doesn't leave a record of the client anywhere but in the preparer's head.


## So Which Should You Choose?


**Choose Hive Tax AI if:**


- Research and planning are the only two jobs you need this platform to do
- You want pricing you can see and calculate before ever getting on a call
- A curated, named strategy library matters to how you sell planning to clients
- Your practice is US-only


**Choose TaxGPT if:**


- You want prep, review, drafting, and client memory covered in the same system that does research
- You handle multi-jurisdiction work
- A SOC 2 Type II attestation is a requirement for your own compliance posture
- Integrations with your existing tax software matter
- You'd rather run one platform than stack and reconcile several SKUs


If you're evaluating the category more broadly, this comparison sits alongside[TaxGPT vs Blue J](https://taxgpt.com/blog/taxgpt-vs-bluej) for firms weighing research-first tools, and additionally TaxGPT vs Bizora AI and TaxGPT vs Juno for firms comparing prep-workflow point tools instead.


Before you decide, run the trial-week test: take the same three research questions and one planning scenario through both. Use Hive's trial and a TaxGPT demo. Score three things: citation quality on the research questions, what happens to the answer after it's generated (does it stay in a chat, or does it become a memo, a file note, a next step), and total cost to cover what your firm actually does in a year, not just the research and planning slice of it.


### FAQ


#### Q: Does Hive Tax AI prepare or review tax returns?


**‍** No. Hive Tax AI's return analysis feeds its planning product, extracting facts to select a strategy, but it doesn't prepare a return or review a completed one. TaxGPT does both: Cowork's agentic workflows prepare returns inside the tax software firms already use, and Agent Andrew reviews completed 1040, 1041, 1065, 1120, and 1120-S returns before sign-off.


#### Q: What's the difference between TaxGPT and Hive Tax AI?


**‍** Hive Tax AI is a research and planning platform built around two SKUs. TaxGPT is an AI Operating System built on its own in-house tax code library, covering research, planning, return prep, completed-return review, drafting, and client intelligence in one platform. Both handle research and planning; TaxGPT covers the rest of the engagement as well.


#### Q: Does Hive Tax AI cover Canadian tax?


**‍** No. Hive's research coverage is US federal and state. TaxGPT covers US federal, state, local, territorial, and treaty layers, plus Canadian tax research including CRA guidance, the Income Tax Act, and provincial rules, all drawn from its in-house tax code library.
